note: Folder names stay axial/coronal/sagittal as published. Anatomical names follow +X anterior, +Y inferior, +Z medial.

labels.anatomy: Medial end of the cochleovestibular nerve mesh.
labels.clinical: The facial nerve is anterosuperior at the fundus.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch175 Surgical Anatomy of the Lateral Skull Base

labels.anatomy: Most lateral scala tympani vertex.
labels.clinical: Opens into the scala tympani; cochlear-implant entry.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Same computed point as the footplate centroid.
labels.clinical: The facial nerve runs directly above it.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Lateral surface point of the scala tympani.
labels.clinical: Basal-turn bulge on the medial wall.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Centroid of the first 360° about the modiolus.
labels.clinical: The promontory overlies the basal turn.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch175 Surgical Anatomy of the Lateral Skull Base

labels.anatomy: Representative point at the oval window, which opens into the vestibule.
labels.clinical: Central chamber of the labyrinth.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Most lateral vertex of the vestibular mesh, used as the canal seed.
labels.clinical: Mastoid landmark; the antrum floor is nearby.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Malleus principal-axis end closer to the membrane centre.
labels.clinical: Tip of the manubrium at the membrane.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Incus principal-axis end closer to the stapes.
labels.clinical: Common site of ossicular erosion.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Centroid of the medial stapes vertex cluster.
labels.clinical: Sits in the oval window.

sources.citation: Francis HW, Niparko JK. Temporal Bone Dissection Guide, 2nd ed, Ch2 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone

labels.anatomy: Centroid of the external auditory canal mesh.
labels.clinical: Lateral opening of the canal.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Centroid of the carotid mesh.
labels.clinical: Petrous carotid. Anterior to the cochlea.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch175 Surgical Anatomy of the Lateral Skull Base

labels.anatomy: Point on the sinus-dura mesh. The jugular bulb is not segmented.
labels.clinical: Posterior limit of mastoidectomy. The mesh still mixes sinus and dura.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Most superior bone vertex near the middle ear.
labels.clinical: Floor of the middle cranial fossa.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Estimated medial to the spine of Henle.
labels.clinical: Largest mastoid air cell. No air-cell mesh yet.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Midpoint between the mastoid segment and the chorda tympani.
labels.clinical: Posterior tympanotomy passes between the facial nerve and the chorda.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Most superior vertex of the vestibular mesh.
labels.clinical: Related to the arcuate eminence on the middle-fossa floor.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch175 Surgical Anatomy of the Lateral Skull Base

labels.anatomy: Most inferior vertex on the posterolateral bone.
labels.clinical: Inferior end of the mastoid.

sources.citation: Francis HW, Niparko JK. Temporal Bone Dissection Guide, 2nd ed, Ch3 Mastoidectomy

labels.anatomy: Estimated inferior to the sigmoid point.
labels.clinical: A high bulb can sit under the middle ear. Not segmented.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear

labels.anatomy: Centerline point at the first bend.
labels.clinical: First genu. The greater superficial petrosal nerve leaves here.

sources.citation: Cummings Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery, 7th ed, Ch126 Anatomy of the Temporal Bone, External Ear, and Middle Ear
